question: A monitoring dashboard needs live metric updates from the server every second. The browser never sends data back except on page load. Which transport fits best?
context: Thousands of browsers, one-directional stream, must work through corporate proxies and reconnect automatically after network blips.

options.label: WebSocket
options.why: Works, but you pay for bidirectional plumbing you do not use, and reconnection/last-event replay must be built by hand.

options.label: Server-Sent Events (SSE)
options.why: SSE is plain HTTP, streams server → client, reconnects automatically with Last-Event-ID and passes through proxies that block WebSocket upgrades. It is the simplest correct tool for one-directional updates.

options.label: Short polling every second
options.why: Thousands of clients × 1 request/second is heavy load for mostly empty responses, and latency is bounded by the poll interval.

options.label: gRPC streaming to the browser
options.why: gRPC streaming needs a gRPC-Web proxy in browsers and adds a toolchain for a problem SSE solves natively.
